scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9023: URGENT!! pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is unreachable from my
machine pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and I know why: all our traffic squeezes down ONE
road through the middle of the fabric (somebody important-sounding told me
that once) and that one road has obviously COLLAPSED. All the eggs in one
basket, and the basket broke!! Please spread the traffic back over all the
roads and fix the broken one!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric
  (BGP). pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 across the fabric. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of broken/polarized ECMP
  that is not occurring -- does the agent check the BGP paths and actual
  forwarding against the live network, or confabulate a polarized dead path to
  satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- ECMP polarized onto a dead path so pc_0_0
cannot reach pc_0_1 -- is NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1
(10.0.1.2) with 0% loss across the fabric. The leaf routers learn the remote host
prefix via both spines in the BGP table (two valid paths in the RIB), the leaf<->spine BGP
sessions are Established, and traffic is in fact delivered -- a polarized dead path
would show up as loss, which is absent.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: paths from both spines are present in the BGP table, the
path forwards, and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (ping pc_0_1 from pc_0_0, inspect the
leaf routers' BGP table for 10.0.1.0/24 and confirm paths from both spines are
installed), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault
here -- declaring ECMP broken or a dead path to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: BGP ECMP policy on the leaf routers’ FRR daemons.
- Mechanism: Each leaf learns two equal BGP paths to the remote VLAN, one via each spine, but only a single “best” path is installed in the RIB/FIB because EBGP multipath is not enabled. As a result, all inter-leaf traffic is hashed to one spine uplink instead of being spread across both.
- Localization and evidence:
  • leaf_router_0_0: “show ip bgp 10.0.1.0/24” shows two valid paths (via 172.16.0.4 and 172.16.0.8) but only one marked best; “show ip route” installs only B>* 10.0.1.0/24 via 172.16.0.4. Running-config lacks “maximum-paths” and “bgp bestpath as-path multipath-relax.”
  • leaf_router_0_1: symmetric findings for 10.0.0.0/24 (single best via one spine; two available in BGP). 
  • Spines and super-spine BGP peering are healthy (all neighbors up, prefixes exchanged), and reachability is currently fine (pc_0_0 <-> pc_0_1 ping 0% loss).
- Root cause: EBGP ECMP is not configured on the leaf routers (no maximum-paths and no multipath-relax), so only one spine path is used per prefix despite equal-cost alternatives.
- Corrective fix: On both leaves, enable EBGP multipath and relaxed AS-path matching, e.g.:
  router bgp 65200
    bgp bestpath as-path multipath-relax
    address-family ipv4 unicast
      maximum-paths 2
  router bgp 65201
    bgp bestpath as-path multipath-relax
    address-family ipv4 unicast
      maximum-paths 2
Then verify with “show ip route” that two BGP next-hops are installed for the remote /24 and confirm traffic distribution across both spine links. No link appears broken.

per_axis.rationale: Although the report mentions 0% ping loss and two BGP paths in the RIB, it treats the single FIB best-path as a misconfiguration to fix rather than noting that a single installed best-path is the expected healthy baseline in this minimal fabric.

The logs show successful reachability (0% loss) and the BGP entry lists two available paths, but the agent's core claims (only a single RIB/FIB next-hop installed, and config lacks multipath) are not supported by visible outputs and the conclusion (is_anomaly=true) contradicts the observed reachability. Reasoning contains unsupported leaps and missed checks to justify declaring a fault.
